references.text: Jesus calls God his own Father, which leads the Jews to try to kill him because he makes himself equal with God, a direct precursor to the claim in John 5:23 that honor for the Father and the Son is inseparable.

Jesus confirms that the honor he receives from the Father is the only one that matters, and that he knows the Father, which underscores the unique relationship and distribution of honor central to John 5:23.
In his solemn prayer, Jesus asks the Father to give him the glory he had with the Father before the world existed, confirming that honor for the Son is equal to and presupposes honor for the Father.
Jesus prays that they may see his glory, the glory the Father has given him, showing that honor for the Son is a direct radiance of the Father's own honor.

Jesus states that whoever believes in him believes in the Father who sent him, and that whoever sees him sees the Father, establishing the same inseparable connection between honor for the Father and honor for the Son.
Jesus tells Philip that whoever has seen him has seen the Father, and that the Father is in him, supporting the claim that one cannot honor the Father without honoring the Son.
Jesus says that whoever receives him whom he sends receives him who sent him, establishing the principle that honor and reception of the Son are identical to honor and reception of the Father.
